rows.scope: Annex I point 3.4.5 'Muscle meat of the following fish:' / 3.4.5.1 'Species other than those listed under 3.4.5.2' - 0,10 mg/kg
rows.basis: wet weight ('The maximum level applies to the wet weight. Where fish are intended to be eaten whole, the maximum level applies to the whole fish.')
rows.evidence: Reg (EU) 2025/1891 Annex point (2) (replacement entry 3.4.5 of Annex I to Reg (EU) 2023/915), row 3.4.5.1 = 0,10; Annex point (1) defines inorganic arsenic as sum of As(III) and As(V) applying to 3.4.1-3.4.8; Article 2 and new Article 10(1)(q). Same text present in consolidated 02023R0915-20251008 (M10).
rows.primary_source_used: http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/32025R1891 (CELLAR XHTML of OJ L 2025/1891, 18.9.2025); cross-checked in consolidated text http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/02023R0915-20251008
rows.note: Compared the primary-text row 3.4.5.1 (0,10 mg/kg wet weight, muscle meat of fish species other than 3.4.5.2) with the register's 100 ug/kg wet-weight row; value, basis and scope agree. Article 2: entry into force on the twentieth day after publication in OJ L of 18.9.2025, i.e. 8 October 2025; Article 1(1)(b) inserts Article 10(1)(q) of Reg (EU) 2023/915 naming 8 October 2025 for points 3.4.5 to 3.4.8. The three later acts amending 2023/915 (Reg (EU) 2026/1825 3-MCPD, 2026/1828 THC, 2026/1890 furan) do not touch section 3.4, so the level is in force on 2026-09-02.

rows.scope: Annex II point 1, Table 1 'General list of migration limits for substances migrating from plastic materials and articles', row 'Aluminium' (salts allowed: yes) SML 1 mg/kg food or food simulant; regulation scope per Article 1(2)/Article 2(1): plastic materials and articles intended to come into contact with food
rows.basis: specific migration limit expressed in mg/kg food or food simulant (Annex II point 1: 'shall not release the substances in Table 1 ... in quantities exceeding the specific migration limits expressed in mg/kg food or simulant')
rows.evidence: Consolidated 02011R0010-20230831 (017.001): Annex II (text marked M15 = Reg (EU) 2020/1245) point 1 Table 1 row 'Aluminium | yes | 1'. Re-read identically in the latest consolidation 02011R0010-20260714 (021.001), whose amending-acts list adds M18 Reg (EU) 2024/3190, M19 Reg (EU) 2025/351, M20 Reg (EU) 2026/245 and M21 Reg (EU) 2026/1380; none changes the aluminium row.
rows.primary_source_used: http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/02011R0010-20230831 (CELLAR XHTML of the consolidation the register cites); cross-checked http://publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/02011R0010-20260714 (current consolidation) and the CELLAR branch notice for 32011R0010 listing consolidated versions
rows.note: Compared the Annex II Table 1 aluminium SML of 1 mg/kg food or food simulant with the register's 1000 ug/kg specific-migration row for plastic food-contact materials and articles; value, basis and scope agree and Regulation (EU) No 10/2011 is in force. The cited 31.08.2023 consolidation is no longer the latest (current consolidation is dated 14.07.2026) but the aluminium row is unchanged; the register note's attribution of the row to Reg (EU) 2016/1416 is a provenance detail I did not read (the current Annex II text is marked as inserted by Reg (EU) 2020/1245) and does not affect the verdict.

rows.scope: Regulation 2.1.1(2) Table, item 8 'Chromium' - 'All fishery products' - 12 (current text); in the 2016-inserted text: item 9 Chromium, '7[All fishery products 12]'
rows.basis: parts per million (mg/kg or mg/L) in the article of food as specified (table header of the current 2.1.1(2) Table); the 2016 insertion used 'parts per million by weight'
rows.successor: Food Safety and Standards (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) First Amendment Regulations, 2020, notification F. No. Stds/SP/(Contaminants)/Notification-1/FSSAI-2018 dated 7 August 2020 (substituted the whole of regulation 2.1.1 including the metal table; the operative text is regulation 2.1.1(2) Table item 8 Chromium of the FSS (Contaminants, Toxins and Residues) Regulations, 2011 as amended, Compendium Version-IX 03.02.2026)
rows.evidence: FSSAI Compendium Version-IX (03.02.2026), regulation 2.1.1(2) Table, item 8 'Chromium - All fishery products - 12', with the entire clause 2.1.1 bracketed as footnote 15 'substituted by F. No. Stds/SP/(Contaminants)/Notification-1/FSSAI-2018, dated 7th August, 2020'. FSSAI Compendium Version-II (18.08.2017), item 9 Chromium, row '7[All fishery products 12]', footnote 7 'Inserted by notification no. F. No. P.15025/264/13-PA/FSSAI, dated the 3rd May, 2016' (the Third Amendment Regulations, 2016).
rows.primary_source_used: https://fssai.gov.in/upload/uploadfiles/files/Comp_Contaminants_Regulations_03_02_2026_IX.pdf (current official consolidation); https://jaivikbharat.fssai.gov.in/pdf/Compendium_Contaminants_Regulations.pdf (Version-II, 18.08.2017, showing the 2016 insertion). The packet gave no register_url and the Gazette PDF named on the source page (raw/regulatory/in/india-fssai-2016-heavy-metals-third-amendment.pdf) is not present in this worktree.
rows.note: The value, scope and basis agree: 12 ppm (12,000 ug/kg) for 'All fishery products' under unspeciated chromium is what the 3 May 2016 Third Amendment inserted (Version-II compendium, footnote 7, item 9 as the register note says) and it is carried verbatim as item 8 in the current table. The verdict is mismatch solely on in-force status: the 2016 instrument's inserted text was replaced when the First Amendment Regulations, 2020 (notified 7 August 2020) substituted the whole of regulation 2.1.1, so the row should cite the 2020 amendment or the consolidated 2011 regulations rather than the superseded 2016 amendment.
